measures.title: Denial of bail for offenses other than murder or treason (Article 1, Section 17)
measures.summary: Indiana's Constitution now lets courts deny bail only to people charged with murder or treason when the proof is evident or the presumption strong. This amendment would let courts also deny bail to a person charged with any other offense if the proof is evident or the presumption strong, and the state proves by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions would reasonably protect the safety of any other person or the community.
measures.yesMeans: You approve amending the Indiana Constitution so judges can deny bail for other offenses when both conditions are met.
measures.noMeans: You reject the amendment; the right to bail stays as it is, with denial allowed only for murder or treason.

measures.title: Residency of city and town court judges (Article 6, Section 6)
measures.summary: This amendment concerns where the judge of a city or town court may live. It would allow such a judge to reside in the county where the court is located, or in the bordering county closest to the city or town where the court is located.
measures.yesMeans: You approve amending the Indiana Constitution to allow city and town court judges to live in the court's county or the closest bordering county.
measures.noMeans: You reject the amendment, and the constitution's residency rule for city and town court judges is not changed.
